q: Does the Heisenberg-scaling claim survive a proper ensemble log-log fit of the post-lock regime, rather than a single-run 1.12x-bound assertion at seed 38?
basis: Current replication reports one representative-run Heisenberg-vs-bound ratio (5981 controlled-U applications, err = 1.87e-4 rad = 1.12x the 1/N_tot bound). The 200-trial scaling ensemble (Experiment B) exists but was only used to show the two-regime plateau/collapse shape; no log-log slope was fit and no ensemble-mean sigma * N_tot(step) constant was reported. Heavy-tailed distribution (Experiment C: 4% below-headline in 50 steps) means single-run scaling could over-state saturation.
next_steps: Reuse the existing experimentB_scaling.json 200 RFPE trajectories: (i) for each trial identify the post-lock step k* where M first exceeds 1; (ii) fit log(err) vs log(sum_M) over k in [k*, 50], report median slope with 25th/75th percentiles; (iii) compute the running product sigma_step * N_tot(step) per trial and plot ensemble median with IQR band — a Heisenberg-saturated protocol keeps this quantity roughly constant. No new sims required.

q: How much of the paper's real Fig. 2a advantage came from the 1000-run classical-simulation average (dashed line) versus the physical chip run (solid), and does our Qiskit-shot replication match the classical-sim curve on a shot-for-shot basis?
basis: The paper plots one representative silicon-photonic experimental run and a separate 1000-run classical-simulation average as a dashed reference. Our replication reaches error 1.87e-4 rad, better than the paper's 2.4e-4 rad; but posterior sigma (1.30e-3 vs 4.2e-4) is 3x larger, suggesting our particle-refit Gaussian and the paper's 1000-particle SMC handle the tails differently. A direct shot-for-shot classical-vs-classical comparison would isolate chip-noise from algorithm-noise.
next_steps: Rerun Experiment A at n_particles = 1000 (the paper's stated particle count) across 1000 seeds, average the per-step median err trajectory, and overlay on the paper's Fig. 2a dashed curve extracted with WebPlotDigitizer. If the two curves overlay to within 20% median-err at every step, the algorithm implementation is confirmed equivalent and the paper's chip-vs-sim gap is a pure hardware-noise story. Free endpoint: local CPU. Wallclock estimate: ~4 h at 20000 particles, ~15 min at 1000 particles.

q: Would the replication hold up under a realistic silicon-photonic experimental noise model (SFWM heralding inefficiency, SNSPD dark counts, thermo-optic phase-shifter drift), or is the current statevector-perfect result a best-case ceiling?
basis: C4 was explicitly deferred. The current code uses the ideal Qiskit statevector — no gate infidelity, no depolarizing T_2, no heralding-loss model, no phase-shifter drift. The paper reports gate-noise sigma_phi ~= 0.3 rad and depolarizing T_2 tolerance as headline claims. Without a noise sweep we cannot distinguish a genuine algorithmic replication from an artifact of the perfect-simulator setting.
next_steps: Extend rfpe_sim.py with three toggles: (i) additive Gaussian jitter on Theta at sigma_phi in {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5} rad; (ii) per-step depolarizing channel of strength p = 1 - exp(-M/T_2) with T_2 in {inf, 100, 30, 10, 3}; (iii) Bernoulli-drop heralding with efficiency eta in {1.0, 0.8, 0.5, 0.2}. Repeat the 200-trial ensemble at each grid point. Test whether the median-final-err curve matches Fig. 3 of the paper. Free endpoint: local CPU, ~1-2 h wallclock at n_particles=5000.

q: Can the replication be extended to a multi-parameter Bayesian phase-estimation setting — jointly estimating two commuting phases Phi_1, Phi_2 in a controlled-U(4) — while preserving Heisenberg scaling per parameter?
basis: The paper's algorithm is scalar: one phase Phi, one Gaussian prior. Recent work (Rudinger et al. 2017, Gebhart et al. 2023) has proposed multi-parameter Bayesian QPE using joint SMC on a product-of-Gaussians prior; the question is whether the Ferrie particle-guess heuristic (M = ceil(1.25/sigma), Theta ~ prior) generalizes with the same convergence rate to a 2-phase setting.
next_steps: Modify rfpe_sim.py: replace scalar Phi with vector Phi = (Phi_1, Phi_2) and controlled-U with a diag(1, e^{i*Phi_1}, e^{i*Phi_2}, e^{i*(Phi_1+Phi_2)}) on a 3-qubit circuit (2 target + 1 control, or interleaved). Extend the prior to a diagonal covariance Gaussian; pick M_i and Theta_i independently per parameter via the same heuristic; refit a joint Gaussian per step. Measure per-parameter final err at 50, 100, 200 steps; check Heisenberg scaling holds on each axis separately. Free endpoint: local CPU. Compare vs Rudinger 2017 multi-parameter scaling bounds.

q: How does swapping the Gaussian SMC prior for a matrix-product-state (MPS) or tensor-network prior affect RFPE convergence in the heavy-tailed low-M plateau regime, especially for stuck runs (73% of seeds in Experiment C did not reach 1e-2 rad in 50 steps)?
basis: Experiment C revealed a bimodal outcome distribution: most runs either escape the M=1 plateau and collapse super-exponentially, or stay stuck. The stuck mode is a known SMC pathology when the Gaussian is a poor approximation to a genuinely bimodal or long-tailed posterior. Tensor-network / MPS priors (Stoudenmire & Schwab 2016, Cheng et al. 2019 for QPE) can represent multi-modal distributions natively and may cure the plateau without needing 20000 particles.
next_steps: Reimplement the prior as a 1-D MPS with bond dimension chi in {2, 4, 8, 16} discretized on 1024 phase bins; keep the Ferrie heuristic for (M, Theta) selection but replace the resample-reweight-refit step with an MPS Bayesian update (Hadamard-product of the likelihood-as-vector into the MPS, then compress). Rerun Experiment C at 100 seeds. Compare (i) median final err at 50 steps, (ii) fraction-below-1e-2 rad, (iii) fraction stuck at plateau. Predict: at chi=8 the stuck-fraction drops from ~73% toward ~10%. Free endpoint: local CPU; use quimb or tenpy for the MPS. No new hardware.
